mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during episodes where both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST falls by >10%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and dampens earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA by >5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods of persistent industrial production contraction as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent collapse in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% signals an abrupt monetary easing in a deflationary environment, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during episodes where both FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL < 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals improving household purchasing power, which boosts consumption and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained above-trend PAYEMS growth as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate above 7% and a fall in average weekly hours (not available, so use PAYEMS and UNRATE interaction as proxy) signals both job loss and underemployment, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during episodes where UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS does not grow month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) of more than 2% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months of >2% monthly decline in real retail sales.
